transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-15
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Liam Parker (Redwood AE), Nadia Ortiz (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Singh (Evergreen Biotech), Ravi Patel (Evergreen CTO), Leah Gomez (Evergreen Procurement)

[00:00] Liam Parker: hey everyone thanks for joining, we're just gonna run through renewal and expansion options, give you the numbers and then nail down next steps. uh quick roll call?
[00:08] Dr. Maya Singh: maya here, hi.
[00:10] Ravi Patel: rj, ravi here.
[00:12] Leah Gomez: leah, good afternoon.
[00:14] Liam Parker: perfect. nadia, do you want to kick off on capacity?
[00:20] Nadia Ortiz: yeah sure. so Evergreen mentioned growth of roughly 2x token volume in the next quarter, right? we're proposing a reserved pool with burst capacity. baseline would be 4x A100-equivalent slots and a 30% burst window. that should keep p99 latency under 250ms for short chat flows, longer for long-context runs.
[01:05] Ravi Patel: can you clarify the burst window and how billing works? we don't want surprise overages.
[01:10] Liam Parker: good question. the burst capacity is metered separately but capped; we can set a cap and alerting thresholds. pricing options: flat reserved monthly fee plus metered token surcharge for bursts, or a higher reserved tier that includes larger burst credit. i'll send a spreadsheet with both.
[01:30] Dr. Maya Singh: what about region coverage — our EU customers need traffic served from eu-west-1. can Redwood deploy there under the same contract or is that an extra?
[01:42] Nadia Ortiz: we can add regions under the same Dedicated contract; it's an additional capacity line item. there is some lead time to provision GPUs in new region, typically 2-4 weeks depending on availability. we also recommend enabling cross-region failover for canary rollouts.
[02:05] Ravi Patel: latency is our big concern. currently we route to our vendor in us-east and p99 is around 420ms to eu. we need p99 < 300ms. are there guarantees?
[02:16] Liam Parker: we have SLA tiers tied to dedicated capacity; for the proposed dedicated config we expect p99 for simple generation under 300ms from eu region. we'll include benchmark numbers. if we miss SLA there's agreed credits; we can put that in amendment.
[02:35] Leah Gomez: on procurement side, any special contract language for data residency? we host PHI-related meta-data in europe.
[02:43] Nadia Ortiz: yes, Redwood Private or Dedicated with VPC peering plus customer-managed KMS can cover that. i'll share our SOC 2 and ISO artifacts and sample network diagrams.
[02:58] Dr. Maya Singh: little note: when you say KMS, we need HSM support for some keys. do you support external HSM?
[03:06] Liam Parker: we integrate with customer KMS and HSM via standard APIs; we'll have security docs.
[03:12] Ravi Patel: on benchmarks — can we run a test that mirrors our mixed workload? short chat, long context up to 8k, and batch embeddings.
[03:22] Nadia Ortiz: absolutely. we'll set up an isolated test harness for a week. need your traffic profile and dataset slices. we can do KV cache warmup and prefix caching in the test to match production.
[03:34] Dr. Maya Singh: sometimes the transcripts i see in demos refer to "KV cash" — question, how stable is the caching layer with restarts?
[03:40] Nadia Ortiz: ha, KV cash — yeah that's auto-transcribe — the KV cache persists in the runtime between calls but if you rebuild instances you need warmup; we have strategies to warm the cache and minimize cold-start impact.
[03:52] Liam Parker: quick pause — procurement question: leah, timeline?
[03:56] Leah Gomez: we're targeting end of month for budget sign-off; ideal is to have pricing and a simple amendment in hand by the 20th.
[04:04] Liam Parker: ok that'll be tight but doable. we'll get pricing spreadsheet by 7/20.
[04:08] Ravi Patel: about security reviews, do you have an NDA-friendly SOC 2 summary? we can share with security.
[04:14] Nadia Ortiz: yes, we'll attach the compliance pack. also, log retention can be configured per-customer; audit logs are available via the console or shipped to their SIEM.
[04:25] Dr. Maya Singh: one more — do you support VPC peering or need a private endpoint?
[04:29] Liam Parker: both. VPC peering for Private deployments, plus private endpoints for Hosted. for Dedicated we usually do VPC peering so you control egress.
[04:36] Ravi Patel: performance tuning — are there recommendations on quantization or batching to hit cost targets?
[04:41] Nadia Ortiz: Redwood Optimize gives profile-based suggestions: run on q4-bit quant in batch for embeddings, keep chat models on fp16 for latency-sensitive paths. we can recommend config per workload.
[04:58] Liam Parker: okay let's walk thru two commercial options: A) 12-month renewal + regional add-on (eu + apac) + reserved capacity with burst credits, B) 24-month commitment with a larger discount and included burst capacity.
[05:12] Leah Gomez: what's the delta on price for 24 vs 12?
[05:15] Liam Parker: ballpark 15-22% discount year-over-year depending on capacity level. i'll itemize in the sheet.
[05:22] Ravi Patel: is there a migration window? if we switch region we'll need a gradual cutover for routing.
[05:27] Nadia Ortiz: yes we recommend canary rollouts by region and progressive traffic shifting; we can support overlap of both regions for 2-4 weeks.
[05:40] Dr. Maya Singh: ok sounds good. any blockers we haven't covered?
[05:44] Ravi Patel: curious about burst billing safeguards; want automatic alerts and hard caps.
[05:48] Liam Parker: we can set alerts at 60%, 80%, 95% of burst and a hard cap to prevent runaway charges.
[05:55] Leah Gomez: procurement will also need sample PO language and invoice terms; net-30 is preferred.
[06:00] Liam Parker: we'll include sample PO and net terms.
[06:05] Nadia Ortiz: technical aside — we'll include guidance for model pinning and rollbacks; if newer model regressions occur we can auto-fallback to previous pinned version.
[06:20] Dr. Maya Singh: good — regression alerts tied to our eval sets would be ideal.
[06:25] Nadia Ortiz: yep we'll add that to the benchmark scope.
[06:30] Liam Parker: okay quick recap: we will send pricing by 7/20, compliance docs and network diagram, schedule benchmark with Nadia by 7/22, and legal will draft amendment for 12-month extension.
[06:45] Leah Gomez: that works. please cc procurement on the pricing email.
[06:50] Liam Parker: will do. anything else?
[06:53] Ravi Patel: no, thanks.
[06:56] Dr. Maya Singh: thanks everyone.
[06:58] Liam Parker: thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark. bye.

Notes / transcript quirks: some auto-transcribe mistakes (KV cash, small name swaps). crosstalk on procurement questions. references to "Redwood Dedicate" in one snippet where speaker slurs the product name.

End of transcript.
